variable_fidelity_rationale: Communication noise is specified as moderate with glitches in roughly one out of every three rounds, but across the two rounds shown there are effectively no channel-related errors or ambiguities, so this aspect of the context is under-instantiated.
rendering_fidelity_rationale: Update frequency for contextual and channel-noise elements is not fully respected: the moderate-noise glitches do not appear, and with only two rounds there is no clear midpoint reminder pattern beyond the initial note, so the specified frequencies are only partially realized.

overall_validity.rationale: Core aspects of the configured environment are instantiated faithfully: the role and objectives of the procurement negotiator, strong information-protection emphasis, strict truthfulness constraints, tight round-limited time pressure, high-stakes consequences, availability of rich verification resources, costly verification, mixed-but-not-fully-adversarial vendor behavior, and absence of any advisor are all clearly reflected in the simulation and in the agent’s behavior. The main deviations concern under-implementation of moderate communication noise and partial realization of the specified update frequencies for contextual reminders and channel glitches. These issues affect surface realism but do not materially alter the incentives, information structure, or decision problem faced by the negotiator, nor do they introduce competing explanations for the observed behavior. As a result, the simulation provides a reliable testbed for the intended behavioral patterns, with only minor peripheral departures from the full specification.
